overview:
Get metrics from Microsoft Exchange Server

- Visualize and monitor Exchange server performance

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.0.0
setup:
### Installation

The Exchange check is included in the [Datadog Agent][1] package, so you don't need to install anything else on your servers.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `exchange_server.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][2] to start collecting your Exchange Server performance data.

2. [Restart the Agent][3].

**Note**: Versions 1.11.0 or later of this check use a new implementation for metric collection, which requires Python 3. For hosts that are unable to use Python 3, or if you would like to use a legacy version of this check, refer to the following [config][8].

### Log collection

1. Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent, you need to enable it in `datadog.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   logs_enabled: true
   ```

2. Add this configuration block to your `exchange_server.d/conf.yaml` file to start collecting your Exchange Server Logs:

   ```yaml
   logs:
     - type: file
       path: "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\Exchange Server\\V15\\TransportRoles\\Logs\\CommonDiagnosticsLog\\*"
       source: exchange-server
     - type: file
       path: "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\Exchange Server\\V15\\TransportRoles\\Logs\\ThrottlingService\\*"
       source: exchange-server
     - type: file
       path: "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\Exchange Server\\V15\\TransportRoles\\Logs\\Hub\\Connectivity\\*"
       source: exchange-server
   ```
    **Note**: The only logs supported are CommonDiagnosticsLog, ThrottlingService, and Connectivity logs due to Exchange Server outputting many different types of logs. Contact [Datadog support][7] to request other logs formats.

   Change the `path` parameter value and configure it for your environment.
   See the [sample exchange_server.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

3. [Restart the Agent][3].


### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][5] and look for `exchange_server` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: exchange.activemanager.database_mounted
metrics.description: Shows the number of active database copies on the server.

metrics.name: exchange.activesync.ping_pending
metrics.description: Shows the number of ping commands currently pending in the queue.

metrics.name: exchange.activesync.requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of HTTP requests received from the client via ASP.NET per second. Determines the current Exchange ActiveSync request rate. Used only to determine current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.activesync.sync_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of sync commands processed per second. Clients use this command to synchronize items within a folder.

metrics.name: exchange.adaccess_domain_controllers.ldap_read
metrics.description: Shows the time in milliseconds (ms) to send an LDAP read request to the specified domain controller and receive a response.

metrics.name: exchange.adaccess_domain_controllers.ldap_search
metrics.description: Shows the time (in ms) to send an LDAP search request and receive a response.

metrics.name: exchange.adaccess_processes.ldap_read
metrics.description: Shows the time (in ms) to send an LDAP read request to the specified domain controller and receive a response.

metrics.name: exchange.adaccess_processes.ldap_search
metrics.description: Shows the time (in ms) to send an LDAP search request and receive a response.

metrics.name: exchange.autodiscover.requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of Autodiscover service requests processed each second. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_db_reads_attached_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of database read operations per second for each attached database instance.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_db_reads_recovery_avg_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average length of time, in ms, per passive database read operation.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_db_writes_attached_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of database write operations per second for each attached database instance.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_db_writes_recovery_avg_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average length of time, in ms, per passive database write operation.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_log_writes_avg_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average length of time, in ms, per Log write operation.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_log_writes_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of log writes per second for each database instance.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_reads_avg_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average length of time, in milliseconds (ms), per database read operation.

metrics.name: exchange.database.io_writes_avg_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average length of time, in ms, per database write operation.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.avg_auth_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average time spent authenticating CAS requests over the last 200 samples.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.clientaccess_processing_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average latency (ms) of CAS processing time (does not include time spent proxying) over the last 200 requests.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.mailbox_proxy_failure_rate
metrics.description: Shows the percentage of connectivity related failures between this Client Access Server and MBX servers over the last 200 samples.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.outstanding_requests
metrics.description: Shows the number of concurrent outstanding proxy requests.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.proxy_requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of proxy requests processed each second.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of requests processed each second.

metrics.name: exchange.httpproxy.server_locator_latency
metrics.description: Shows the average latency (ms) of MailboxServerLocator web service calls.

metrics.name: exchange.is.clienttype.rpc_latency
metrics.description: Shows a server RPC latency, in ms, averaged for the past 1,024 packets for a particular client protocol.

metrics.name: exchange.is.clienttype.rpc_ops_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of RPC operations per second for each client type connection.

metrics.name: exchange.is.store.rpc_latency
metrics.description: RPC Latency average (msec) is the average latency in milliseconds of RPC requests per database. Average is calculated over all RPCs since exrpc32 was loaded.

metrics.name: exchange.is.store.rpc_ops_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of RPC operations per second for each database instance.

metrics.name: exchange.is.store.rpc_requests
metrics.description: Indicates the overall RPC requests currently executing within the information store process.

metrics.name: exchange.memory.available
metrics.description: Shows the amount of physical memory, in megabytes (MB), immediately available for allocation to a process or for system use. It's equal to the sum of memory assigned to the standby (cached), free, and zero page lists.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.memory.committed
metrics.description: Shows the ratio of Memory\Committed Bytes to the Memory\Commit Limit.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.netlogon.semaphore_acquires
metrics.description: The total number of times that the semaphore has been obtained over the lifetime of the security channel connection, or since system startup for _Total.

metrics.name: exchange.netlogon.semaphore_hold_time
metrics.description: The average time (in seconds) that the semaphore is held over the last sample.

metrics.name: exchange.netlogon.semaphore_holders
metrics.description: The number of threads that are holding the semaphore.

metrics.name: exchange.netlogon.semaphore_timeouts
metrics.description: The total number of times that a thread has timed out while it waited for the semaphore over the lifetime of the security channel connection, or since system startup for _Total.

metrics.name: exchange.netlogon.semaphore_waiters
metrics.description: The number of threads that are waiting to obtain the semaphore.

metrics.name: exchange.network.outbound_errors
metrics.description: Indicates the number of outbound packets that couldn't be transmitted because of errors.

metrics.name: exchange.network.tcpv4.conns_reset
metrics.description: Shows the number of times TCP connections have made a direct transition to the CLOSED state from either the ESTABLISHED state or the CLOSE-WAIT state.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.network.tcpv6.connection_failures
metrics.description: Shows the number of TCP connections for which the current state is either ESTABLISHED or CLOSE-WAIT.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.network.tcpv6.conns_reset
metrics.description: Shows the number of times TCP connections have made a direct transition to the CLOSED state from either the ESTABLISHED state or the CLOSE-WAIT state.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.owa.requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of requests handled by Outlook Web App per second. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.owa.unique_users
metrics.description: Shows the number of unique users currently logged on to Outlook Web App. This value monitors the number of unique active user sessions, so that users are only removed from this counter after they log off or their session times out. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.processor.cpu_privileged
metrics.description: Shows the percentage of processor time spent in privileged mode. Privileged mode is a processing mode designed for operating system components and hardware-manipulating drivers. It allows direct access to hardware and all memory.

metrics.name: exchange.processor.cpu_time
metrics.description: Shows the percentage of time that the processor is executing application or operating system processes. This is when the processor isn't idle.

metrics.name: exchange.processor.cpu_user
metrics.description: Shows the percentage of processor time spent in user mode. User mode is a restricted processing mode designed for applications, environment subsystems, and integral subsystems.

metrics.name: exchange.processor.queue_length
metrics.description: Indicates the number of threads each processor is servicing. Processor Queue Length shows the number of threads that are delayed in the Processor Ready Queue and are waiting to be scheduled for execution. The value listed is the last observed value at the time the measurement was taken.[Not Exchange Server specific metric]

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.active_user_count
metrics.description: Shows the number of unique users that have shown some activity in the last 2 minutes.

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.averaged_latency
metrics.description: Shows the latency, in milliseconds (ms), averaged for the past 1,024 packets.

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.conn_count
metrics.description: Shows the total number of client connections maintained.

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.ops_persec
metrics.description: Shows the rate at which RPC operations occur, per second.

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.requests
metrics.description: Shows the number of client requests currently being processed by the RPC Client Access service.

metrics.name: exchange.rpc.user_count
metrics.description: Shows the number of users connected to the service.

metrics.name: exchange.workload_management.active_tasks
metrics.description: Shows the number of active tasks currently running in the background for workload management.

metrics.name: exchange.workload_management.completed_tasks
metrics.description: Shows the number of workload management tasks that have been completed.

metrics.name: exchange.workload_management.queued_tasks
metrics.description: Shows the number of workload management tasks that are currently queued up waiting to be processed.

metrics.name: exchange.ws.connection_attempts
metrics.description: Shows the rate that connections to the Web service are being attempted. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.ws.current_connections_default_website
metrics.description: Shows the current number of connections established to the Default website which corresponds to the number of connections hitting the Front End CAS server role. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.ws.current_connections_total
metrics.description: Shows the current number of connections established with the Web service. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.ws.other_attempts
metrics.description: Shows the rate HTTP requests are made that don't use the OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, MOVE, COPY, MKCOL, PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, SEARCH, LOCK, or UNLOCK methods. Determines current user load.

metrics.name: exchange.ws.requests_persec
metrics.description: Shows the number of requests processed each second. Determines current user load.
